clue.text: Feeling sad having toothache?

definitions.meaning: glum, dejected, with a drooping face
jokingly, suffering pain somewhere within one's jaws

explanation.surface: Someone with a throbbing tooth is understandably miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means dejected, while taken literally it places the trouble inside the jaws where a sore tooth sits.

clue.text: A long way from being aloof

explanation.surface: Someone is far removed from being standoffish.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both physical remoteness and an unfriendly, reserved coolness.

clue.text: Elementary prognostication

parts.note: elementary seems to mean simple, but here it means concerning the elements, i.e. wind, rain and sun, and the prediction is about them

explanation.surface: A basic, simple prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorological prediction foretells what the elements (wind, rain, sunshine) will do.

clue.text: I want the lot presumably in the same place

parts.note: at an auction, a bidder making an offer wants the lot on sale, so this is to bid

explanation.surface: A greedy person wants everything, apparently in one spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lot' is an auction item, not 'everything'. Ibid. is the Latin footnote abbreviation for ibidem.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibid. abbreviates the Latin ibidem, used in references to point back to the source just cited.

clue.text: A learner under canvas had natural gift

indicators.note: being under canvas means camping inside a tent, so the other letters go within

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner camping out turned out to have a natural flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under canvas' is the camping idiom: A and L go inside TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A flair or innate aptitude for something is a talent.

clue.text: Went off and destroyed the theory?

definitions.meaning: blew up, as a bomb does
discredited an idea, showed it to be false

explanation.surface: Something blew up and wrecked a hypothesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing up describes a bomb detonating, and a debunked notion is called blown apart in the same word.

clue.text: Censure work for one in Birmingham

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the nickname of the city

parts.note: Brum is the colloquial name for Birmingham, a large English city
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Disapproval of a job someone does in the West Midlands city.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUM is the everyday nickname of Birmingham, England's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: Opprobrium is harsh public criticism or disgrace, a strong form of condemnation.

clue.text: Troops that have been grounded?

parts.note: grounded suggests troops confined to barracks, but the joke is soldiers tied to their own land, a reserve force for home territory

explanation.surface: Soldiers who have been confined or punished.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the British volunteer reserve army, now the Army Reserve; 'grounded' plays on territory meaning land.
explanation.definitionFit: A British reserve force of part-time volunteers, named for defending home soil.

clue.text: Be ambitious but get false praise

indicators.note: false here means not genuine, so the word praise is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ambitious receives only insincere flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim high or long for achievement is to have ambition.

clue.text: Plausible story about one dog

indicators.note: about means around, so the story's word wraps the article

parts.note: a spiel is a glib, persuasive patter
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A convincing tale concerning a single dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plausible story' reads like the definition, but the dog is the answer; the patter wraps the article for 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of gundog with long drooping ears, such as the cocker.

clue.text: Surprisingly pays up about mid-afternoon for old writing material

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters wrap the middle letter
surprisingly signals that the letters of pays up come out in an unexpected order
mid asks for the centre letter of the word afternoon

explanation.surface: Someone unexpectedly settles the bill mid-afternoon to buy antique paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges PAYSUP to PAPYUS; 'about' puts R, the middle of 'afternoon' (flagged by 'mid'), inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptians wrote on sheets made from a reed, the forerunner of paper.

clue.text: Gash yellow partly greyish

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wound that is yellow in part and also grey in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is pale grey, so something coloured like ash is pale grey.

clue.text: Our time

parts.note: the present era as counted from the birth of Christ, the Latin phrase meaning in the year of our Lord

explanation.surface: The age we live in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase dates the current calendar era; 'Our' echoes 'our Lord' in its meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Dates in the common Christian era are labelled with this Latin phrase, AD.

clue.text: Be in no hurry to avoid exertion

explanation.surface: Someone advised to slow down so as not to overdo things.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both to relax one's pace and to rest instead of working hard.

clue.text: No end of sauce found on one's teeth

indicators.note: no end of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: tartare is a mayonnaise sauce served with fish

explanation.surface: Endless amounts of sauce stuck around somebody's teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'lots of' but takes the final E off TARTARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard calcified plaque deposits on dental enamel are called this.

clue.text: Be afraid certain people are frightful

parts.note: to fear is to be afraid
some means certain unspecified people

explanation.surface: Being scared, some find particular people terrifying.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something alarming that inspires dread.

clue.text: One won't agree to have one

definitions.text: One won't agree to have one

parts.words: One won't agree to have one
parts.note: a person who refuses to agree with another ends up in a dispute

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly refuses to accept something.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'One' is a person; the second is the thing that disagreement brings about, a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Disagreement leads to a row or quarrel, which is a dispute between people.

clue.text: Man shortly came across some lines in mathematics

parts.note: Geo. is the short form of the name George
to meet is to come across, so came across is met
Ry is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A fellow briefly found some lines in a maths lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines are railway lines, RY; geometry is a branch of mathematics, the definition being by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of maths dealing with shapes, angles and lines.

clue.text: Spare part for motorist to obtain without question

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so obtain's word goes round question's

parts.note: to get is to obtain
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A driver gets a replacement part without being asked anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'not having' but here carries its old sense of outside, so the verb for obtain goes round the verb for question.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal between engine parts, a common replacement for car owners.

clue.text: After almost 30 days, I take alternative being of lower rank

indicators.note: after places the I and the alternative following the shortened month
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the month goes

parts.note: June is a month of thirty days
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: After nearly a month, I choose another option despite being outranked.
explanation.walkthrough: '30 days' is June ('thirty days hath September, April, June and November'); 'almost' trims it to JUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A subordinate or younger person holds a position beneath others.

clue.text: Determine to do the crossword again

definitions.meaning: work out the puzzle once more, solve it a second time

explanation.surface: Someone vows to tackle the puzzle a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to decide, and split as re-solve it means to work out a second time.

clue.text: Vigorously like this goat round at the bottom

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the end, so the round letter comes last

parts.note: a billy is a male goat
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A goat circles energetically at the foot of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like billy-o' is a British phrase meaning with great energy, so 'like this' completes the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom like billy-o means with great energy or intensity.

clue.text: Printed notes

parts.note: notes suggests written jottings or banknotes, but these are musical notes on paper

explanation.surface: Typed memos or banknotes fresh off the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical scores printed on paper for performers to read.

clue.text: Sign there is more to follow

explanation.surface: A signal that something else is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol for addition, and the word meaning in addition, as in additionally.

clue.text: Hear that Cain's brother can

definitions.note: can is a verb, the answer an adjective: can means is able

indicators.note: hear that tells the solver that a word is spoken out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: Abel was the brother Cain killed in Genesis

explanation.surface: Listen to how capable the biblical brother is.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Cain murdered his brother Abel.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the capacity to do something is what 'can' expresses.

clue.text: Give out spurious name at early start

indicators.note: spurious means false, so the letters of name at are rearranged
start picks the first letter of early

explanation.surface: Invent a false name right at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spurious' rearranges NAMEAT to EMANAT; 'start' gives E from 'early'.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit or issue forth, as a smell or a light does.

clue.text: Generous old party

definitions.meaning: the British party that preceded today's ... Democrats

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted elderly person.
explanation.walkthrough: The British Liberal Party merged into the Liberal Democrats in 1988; 'old party' looks like an elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means free-giving and names the former British political party of Gladstone.

clue.text: One not expected to be found out

definitions.text: One not expected to be found out

parts.words: One not expected to be found out
parts.note: found out looks like caught or exposed, but means discovered away from home

explanation.surface: Someone unlikely to be caught or exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A homebody who prefers staying indoors is rarely seen outside.
